title: Coconut-Lime Cod Chowder with Sweet Corn, Baby Potatoes & Spinach
summary: Mild, dairy-free fish chowder with tender cod, sweet corn, potatoes, spinach, and a little lime. About 40 minutes total, 20–25 minutes active.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb kosher cod or haddock fillets, skinless and boneless, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
1 1/4 lb baby Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
2 cups baby spinach, washed and checked as appropriate
1 can (13.5 oz) unsweetened light coconut milk
Optional: chopped cilantro or parsley, and pareve crusty bread for dipping
instructions: In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add onion, celery, and bell pepper; sauté for 5–6 minutes until beginning to soften. Add garlic and paprika for 30 seconds.
Add diced potatoes, vegetable broth, and light coconut milk. Bring to a simmer, cover partially, and cook for 12–15 minutes until potatoes are almost fork-tender.
Add corn and fish pieces. Keep at a gentle simmer for 5–7 minutes, without vigorous stirring, until fish is opaque, flakes easily, and reaches 145°F in the thickest piece.
Stir in spinach for 1–2 minutes until wilted. Season with salt and pepper. Add 1–2 tsp lime juice to the pot, offering more at the table.
Serve in bowls, with optional pareve crusty bread. For children, lift out pieces of fish, potatoes, and corn and serve separately with a little broth.
child_friendly_modifications: Keep the lime subtle and omit any spicy seasoning. Serve tender fish flakes, soft potato pieces, and sweet corn in separate sections if preferred. Carefully check fish for bones, break into small pieces, and cool broth thoroughly. For children who prefer dipping, offer pareve toast alongside.
leftovers: Cool promptly in shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours. Use within 1–2 days for best fish texture; reheat gently to 165°F without boiling hard, which can toughen the fish. Add a splash of broth when reheating. Do not leave at room temperature.
